title: Incident-bot: notify #incidents when overload protection activates (shed/admission control)
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Add structured incident-bot notifications when hot-route capacity protection activates so on-call can quickly distinguish expected best-effort shedding from enterprise-impacting overload events.

We need notifications for:
- sustained admission control (best-effort gated) on protected routes
- shed-rate threshold exceeded (active dropping) on protected routes

Primary destination: #incidents (and optionally #eng-oncall as a lower-noise mirror for early canary). Notifications must be deduped, rate-limited, and include links to the relevant dashboard + runbook section.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Incident-bot posts a structured message when any protected route group enters ACTIVE protection state for >= 5 minutes (configurable).
2) Message includes: region, route_group, tier breakdown (enterprise vs best-effort), trigger type (admission_control vs shedding), current shed_rate, queue_depth/scheduler_lag summary, and the evaluated threshold.
3) Message includes deep links to: Hot-route protection dashboard and overload protection runbook.
4) Dedupe: do not post more frequently than once per 15 minutes per (region, route_group, trigger_type). Post a 'resolved' message when protection clears for >= 10 minutes.
5) Works in dry-run mode (logs only) behind a feature flag, with per-region enablement.
6) Security: no tenant/customer identifiers in Slack payload; only route group + tier + region. Access to any debug detail remains in internal tools.
implementation_notes:
Source of truth for triggers is the overload protection aggregator (metrics-derived) rather than raw per-request events to avoid high-cardinality spam.

Trigger signals (already emitted by routing/runtime):
- overload_protection_state{region, route_group, tier} = ACTIVE|INACTIVE
- shed_rate{region, route_group, tier}
- admission_control_drop_rate{region, route_group, tier}
- runtime_queue_depth_p95{region, route_group}
- scheduler_lag_ms_p95{region, route_group}

Incident-bot changes:
- New rule type: HOT_ROUTE_PROTECTION_ACTIVATION
- New message template with consistent fields + footer links
- Dedupe keys: region + route_group + trigger_type (ignore tier in dedupe to reduce spam)
- Summary calculation: include enterprise + best-effort values in one message; do not page on best-effort-only activation unless it exceeds an absolute shed threshold AND queue depth indicates shared pool risk.

Message format (Slack blocks):
- Title: "Hot-route protection ACTIVE: {route_group} ({region})"
- Fields:
  - Trigger: shedding|admission_control|both
  - Enterprise shed/drop: X% (threshold Y%)
  - Best-effort shed/drop: X% (threshold Y%)
  - Queue depth p95 / Scheduler lag p95
  - Duration in ACTIVE state
- Links:
  - Dashboard: Hot-route Protection (filtered by region + route_group)
  - Runbook: Overload protection & admission control (triage section)

Config:
- feature flag: incident_bot.hot_route_protection_notifications
- per-region allowlist: us-east, eu-west initially
- channel routing: canary -> #eng-oncall; GA -> #incidents

Testing:
- Unit tests for dedupe window + resolved notifications
- Integration test in staging with synthetic ACTIVE/INACTIVE transitions (no real load required).
rollout_plan:
1) Land incident-bot PR with flag default OFF.
2) Enable in staging for synthetic transitions; verify message formatting + links.
3) Canary in us-east to #eng-oncall for 48 hours; validate noise level during expected best-effort shedding.
4) Enable #incidents posting in us-east; then eu-west after 1 week.
5) Document operational expectations in runbook and alert playbook: incident-bot notification is informational, paging still driven by SLO burn alerts (ENG-4926).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Slack noise / paging storms if we post on transient blips.
Mitigation: sustained-active threshold, dedupe windows, and 'best-effort-only' suppression.

Risk: Accidental leakage of customer identifiers if we include tenant labels.
Mitigation: enforce an allowlist of fields; drop/strip any labels other than region/route_group/tier; security review required.

Risk: Broken dashboard links due to query param mismatch.
Mitigation: link to a stable dashboard with optional params; verify in staging and during canary.

comments: On-call requirement: we need a single place to look when protection flips on. SLO burn alerts are too slow for initial triage; this should be the early heads-up, not a page. (Rafael)
Please do NOT include customer/account info in Slack. Route group + tier is enough; escalation can use internal tooling. (Kaitlyn)

Noise concern: best-effort shedding will be common during peak. The rule should only notify #incidents when enterprise tier is impacted OR when best-effort shedding correlates with rising queue depth (risk to shared pools). (Peter)
Copy request: use 'capacity protection' and 'admission control' terminology; avoid 'throttling customers' phrasing. (Sergio)
Game day outcome: notifications were clear and deduped properly; resolved message was especially helpful for declaring recovery. (Rafael)
